question: Can procedural environment map rebuilds avoid testing every radiance proxy for every cube texel while producing identical pixel values?
hypothesis: Conservative 16px cube-direction tiles cull only proxies whose threshold cannot intersect a tile, preserving contribution order and map values while lowering CPU rebuild time.

conditions.profile: CI run 35778003031: environment CPU max 590.7ms; 1080p completed 28.77fps, GPU p95 20.57ms

acceptance.correctness: For every face/mip texel, every proxy with dot(direction, proxy.dir)>threshold remains in its original order; renderer visual and Stanford gates remain within baseline.
acceptance.cpu: Report median full-scan vs tiled proxy accumulation on same 128-proxy fixture and remeasure environment CPU spikes in GPU CI.
acceptance.runtime: Track 1080p completed FPS and GPU p95; do not claim GPU improvement from CPU-only culling.

evidence: local property test on mip edges passed, 13 profile-related tests passed
synthetic 128-proxy, seven-mip fixture: 67,104,768 -> 10,366,864 dot checks; paired medians 1016.54 -> 339.07 ms, accumulated contribution exactly equal

GPU runs 35779130948 and 35781331938: Stanford held-out had no regressions; procedural cubemap keeps 256px/mip, tile property oracle passes; final map computed once after unrelated deformation invalidation was fixed.
decision: Retain conservative 16px direction tiles. Exact contribution sums and no false exclusions; synthetic CPU median 1016.54 -> 339.07ms, while end-to-end scene FPS depends on cache invalidation policy.
